thread.title: Bill Gates to Testify Before House Committee on Jeffrey Epstein Investigation
thread.title_full: Bill Gates to Testify Before House Committee on Jeffrey Epstein Investigation

author: Ethan Brooks
title: Bill Gates to Testify Before House Committee on Jeffrey Epstein Investigation
text:
Bill Gates is scheduled to appear before the House Oversight Committee in June, marking the latest development in a wide-ranging congressional investigation into the network and conduct of the late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein. The billionaire and philanthropist, who has consistently denied any knowledge of Epstein’s crimes, will participate in a closed-door transcribed interview on June 10.
While Gates is moving forward with his appearance, other high-profile figures are facing legal friction. Former Attorney General Pam Bondi will not appear for her scheduled deposition on April 14, despite being subpoenaed in March to discuss her role in the release of Epstein-related files. The discrepancy in cooperation highlights the tension within the committee as it attempts to map the full extent of Epstein’s influence and the government’s handling of his records.
The investigation is drawing on a massive trove of Department of Justice documents that have already implicated numerous influential figures. For Gates, the scrutiny stems from his appearance in these files thousands of times, which include allegations of meetings with Epstein after the financier’s 2008 conviction for sex crimes involving minors and reports of travel on Epstein’s private aircraft.
The Legal Stand-Off Over Pam Bondi
The committee’s attempt to secure testimony from former Attorney General Pam Bondi has hit a roadblock. In a letter to committee chair Rep. James Comer, a Republican from Kentucky, Assistant Attorney General Patrick Davis stated that the Department of Justice believes the subpoena no longer obligates Bondi to appear on April 14 because she can no longer testify in her official capacity as Attorney General.
This position has drawn sharp criticism from the committee’s top Democrat, Rep. Robert Garcia of California. Garcia has called for Bondi to testify immediately, warning that the committee may pursue contempt charges if she defies the subpoena. He emphasized that the survivors of Epstein’s abuse deserve justice, framing her absence as a failure of accountability.
The House Oversight Committee has indicated it will contact Bondi’s personal counsel to negotiate a new schedule for her deposition, though no date has been confirmed.
Scrutiny of the Gates-Epstein Connection
Bill Gates’ cooperation comes amid a flood of evidence documenting his interactions with the disgraced financier. A spokesperson for Gates stated that he “welcomes the opportunity to appear before the Committee,” adding that while Gates “never witnessed or participated in any of Epstein’s illegal conduct, he is looking forward to answering all the committee’s questions.”
However, the DOJ files paint a complex picture. Gates reportedly met with Epstein multiple times after Epstein’s 2008 conviction and used his private plane. Further scrutiny has focused on emails in which Epstein claimed to have helped Gates obtain medication for a sexually transmitted infection acquired from “sex with Russian girls,” and suggested that Gates attempted to provide the same medication to his now ex-wife, Melinda French Gates, in secret.
Melinda French Gates previously described the revelation of these documents as a source of “unbelievable sadness,” noting that they reminded her of the struggles within her marriage. She has maintained that any remaining questions regarding the relationship should be answered by those involved, including her former husband.
A Growing List of Witnesses
The committee is continuing to call a wide array of figures to understand the inner workings of Epstein’s operation. The upcoming schedule includes several key individuals who may provide insight into the financier’s associates and the failures of his incarceration.
| Witness | Status/Date | Context |
|---|---|---|
| Ted Waitt | April 30 | Alleged relationship with Ghislaine Maxwell |
| Howard Lutnick | May 6 | Voluntary testimony |
| Tova Noel | May 18 | Officer guarding Epstein the night he died |
| Bill Gates | June 10 | Closed-door transcribed interview |
| The Clintons | Testified (Feb) | Denied knowledge of crimes prior to 2008 |
The Role of the Inner Circle
Among those who have already testified are figures considered part of Epstein’s closest professional circle. Richard Kahn, Epstein’s former accountant, was mentioned more than 50,000 times in the files. Kahn, whose firm HBRK Associates Inc. Managed Epstein’s finances and medical reimbursements for the girls, testified in March that he was “not aware” of the crimes.
Similarly, Darren Indyke, a longtime personal attorney and co-executor of Epstein’s estate, testified in March that he had “no knowledge whatsoever” of the abuse. Indyke had previously been flagged by a bank for “structured cash transactions” designed to avoid federal reporting requirements.
The Maxwell Deadlock
The committee’s most significant witness, Ghislaine Maxwell, remains a point of contention. Convicted of sex-trafficking and currently serving a 20-year sentence, Maxwell refused to testify during her February deposition, invoking her Fifth Amendment rights. Her legal team has suggested she would only provide the “unfiltered truth” in exchange for immunity or a presidential pardon.
The committee has also deposed former Attorney General Bill Barr and former Labor Secretary Alex Acosta, both of whom played roles in the legal landscape surrounding Epstein’s initial 2008 non-prosecution agreement.
This reporting is based on official committee records and Department of Justice filings. Information regarding legal proceedings is provided for informational purposes and does not constitute legal advice.
The next critical checkpoint for the investigation will be the April 30 deposition of Ted Waitt, followed by the May appearances of Howard Lutnick and Tova Noel, before the committee moves to its June interview with Bill Gates.
We invite readers to share their thoughts on the committee’s progress in the comments below.
summary: Bill Gates is scheduled to appear before the House Oversight Committee in June, marking the latest development in a wide-ranging congressional investigation into the network and conduct of the late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein. Former Attorney General Pam Bondi will not appear for her scheduled deposition on April 14, despite being subpoenaed in March to discuss her role in the release of Epstein-related files.
